objective: T-20260930-01: does the Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone 60/40 rebalancing-pressure signal (Threshold averaged over 25 deltas 0.1%..2.5%, Calendar last-week signal, weight W = 0.6*(-Threshold/0.012) + 0.4*CalendarMod), simulated from SPY and IEF closes, still forecast next-day SPY returns in the part a next-open fill can capture (the open-to-close leg) in 2016-2026 and in the 2024-01-08..2026-09-29 window, and does an equity-leg-only book (SPY, QQQ, TQQQ/SQQQ) clear a net Sharpe of 0.8 after 10 bp per side? sources.core_claim: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone (NBER w33554, March 2025, revised January 2026, full text read): a one-standard-deviation increase in the Threshold (Calendar) signal lowers next-day S&P 500 futures returns by about 16 (17) bp and raises 10-year Treasury futures returns by 4 (2) bp; the pressure reverts within two weeks; Section 4 front-running spread portfolio (long S&P 500 futures / short 10y note futures, weight = average of modified Threshold and Calendar signals) has Sharpe above 1 over 1997-2023.
sources.project_applicability: Source of the Threshold and Calendar signal definitions, the next-day sign expectation (equity down when equity is overweight) and the two-week reversion horizon used to set the placebo shift range.
sources.reflection: Futures returns, close-to-close, not open-to-close; author-reported Sharpe with the authors' own cost estimate; multiple-comparison bias on signal windows flagged by the discussant; effect concentrated before the 2016 start of the local sample is not excluded.

sources.core_claim: NBER abstract page (revision date January 2026): institutional rebalancing has a market-wide impact; equity returns fall 17 bp over the next day when stocks are overweight; cost to investors about 16 billion USD a year.
sources.project_applicability: Headline effect size the negation regression is measured against (the effect is a close-to-close 17 bp, larger than a 10 bp per side cost).

sources.core_claim: Paper Section 4 defines the modified Calendar signal as sign(-Calendar) in the last week (5 days) of a month, a reversal term sign(Calendar_{-4}) on the first business day of the new month, and zero on any other day; the Threshold part is rescaled to -Threshold/1.5% so both signals have equal risk contribution.
sources.project_applicability: Fixes the Calendar structure (last-week days plus one reversal day). The queue task and the QuantReturns replication use normalisation 0.012 and put the reversal on the last session of the month; the preregistration follows the task.
sources.reflection: Paper normalises by 1.5%, QuantReturns by 0.012, and the paper places the reversal on the first business day; the preregistered candidate uses the task's version and the difference is a disclosed deviation.

sources.core_claim: Parker, Schoar and Sun (NBER w28028, JF 2023): target date funds rebalance contrarianly between stocks and bonds within a few months; the flows reach stocks held through mutual funds and reduce their next-quarter returns.
sources.project_applicability: Independent evidence that the rebalancing flow exists and is spread over months, so a next-day-only signal captures only part of it.
sources.reflection: Quarterly horizon, cross-sectional stock effect; not a daily index timing rule; no Sharpe.

existing_solution_comparison: Published: NBER w33554 (Sharpe 1.11 futures spread 1997-09..2023-03, 0.90 excluding 2008-09..2009-03 and 2020-03, roughly 1 net of authors' cost estimate) and QuantReturns independent replication (futures 1.42 2007..2025-06, SPY/TLT ETF version Sharpe 1.17, Beta 0.12, no costs, both legs traded). Not enough for us: both are close-to-close futures spreads with a bond leg (owner rejected cross-asset 2026-09-28), untradable at Alpaca as futures, and neither reports the overnight/intraday split or costs at a next-open fill. Local work fills exactly that gap: the equity leg only, ETF closes, open-to-close return, 10 bp per side.
